title.narrative: Global Learning Hub - Women’s Voice and Leadership Learning Partnership
Pôle d’apprentissage mondial – Partenariat d’apprentissage Voix et leadership des femmes

description.narrative:
IDRC is partnering with Global Affairs Canada to assist its renewed Women’s Voice and Leadership (WVL) program to increase the impacts of more than 2,200 women’s rights organizations (WROs), LGBTQI+ groups and feminist movements across regions. Through peer-learning, evidence gathering and organizational strengthening, the WVL Learning Partnership will equip these groups to better achieve change that is needed and to challenge harmful and discriminatory social beliefs and practices where they exist and hinder gender equality.
These organizations and movements have valuable local knowledge and experience, but there’s often no strong system to connect them or share lessons across regions. Because of this, WROs and LGBTQI+ groups often have to start from scratch instead of learning from what worked—or didn’t—for others. Efforts and campaigns are fragmented, which makes it hard to build a solid evidence base to fight well-organized, global anti-rights narratives. The WVL Learning Partnership is coming at the right time. It offers real-time learning and testing, backed by data and evidence that show what works and why this work matters.
The Global Learning Hub will be coordinated by three feminist organizations that will co-create and sustain, over four years, a feminist, multilingual, and dynamic platform for evidence generation, knowledge sharing, and community-led learning - rooted in the lived experiences and activism of the organisations at the forefront of the work to advance gender equality and human rights. At its core, the Hub will co-create and deliver a feminist agenda with these 2,200 organisations, ensuring that their questions, priorities and capacities shape the foundation of research. It will also facilitate peer-led learning to build collective resilience and facilitate a learning between communities – which will result in increased effectiveness, solidarity, reflection, and coordinated action. Finally, the Hub will be well positioned to synthesize, translate and amplify feminist knowledge and evidence from the 2,200 organisations into creative, multilingual formats that inform advocacy and deepen intersectional analysis. This will result ultimately in less discrimination and the ability for women and LGBTQI+ organisations to promote a future based on equality and inclusion. Ultimately, this collaboration with Global Affairs Canada will ensure that Canada’s international assistance in support to WROs, LGBTQI+ groups and their networks works effectively and achieves real change.
